faq.q: Is a gift deed mandatory for gifting mutual funds to a sibling?
faq.a: While some AMCs might not strictly demand it for transfers between specified relatives, a notarised Gift Deed is highly recommended. It serves as crucial evidence of the gift and relationship, especially for tax purposes.

faq.q: Are there any charges for gifting mutual fund units?
faq.a: Generally, AMCs or RTAs do not levy any direct charges for the off-market transfer of mutual fund units between relatives. However, you might incur costs for drafting and notarising the Gift Deed.

faq.q: What if my sibling is an NRI?
faq.a: Gifting to an NRI sibling is possible, but it involves additional compliance with FEMA regulations. The NRI sibling must have a valid NRO or NRE account linked to their mutual fund folio, and the transfer usually involves specific declarations.

faq.q: Can I gift an ongoing SIP to my sibling?
faq.a: No, an ongoing SIP cannot be transferred. The gift pertains only to the accumulated units held in your folio. If your sibling wishes to continue investing, they must start a new SIP from their own bank account.

faq.q: How is capital gains tax calculated for the recipient of the gift?
faq.a: The recipient's cost of acquisition is considered as the original cost at which the donor purchased the units. The holding period for calculating capital gains also starts from the donor's original purchase date.

faq.q: Are there any limits on the value of mutual fund units I can gift to my sibling?
faq.a: No, there are no monetary limits on the value of mutual fund units you can gift to your sibling. Gifts to specified relatives are fully exempt from income tax for the recipient, regardless of the amount.
